sections.title: Principles of Injury & Violence Prevention
sections.description: This course will introduce students to the principles of injury and violence prevention broadly with a focus on understanding study designs used in injury and violence research, and important concepts used in designing, analyzing, and interpreting these studies to prioritize evidence-based prevention strategies. Students will analyze injury/violence as a preventable public health issue by synthesizing information on historical, cultural, systemic, and structural causes. Students will use public-access injury and violence data, peer- reviewed literature and other credible resources to identify the magnitude of the problem to the degree that it is known, describe injury/violence problems based on specific sub-populations, assess associated consequences to individuals, families, and communities and critique prevention and intervention strategies. Finally, students will have the opportunity to focus on one specific injury/violence topic and delve into its problem, causes, and public health intervention/prevention best practices.

sections.title: Principles of Injury & Violence Prevention
sections.description: This course will introduce students to the principles of injury and violence prevention broadly with a focus on the various study designs used in injury and violence research, and important concepts used in designing, analyzing, and interpreting these studies. The course will analyze analyze injury/violence as a preventable public health issue by synthesizing information on historical, cultural, systemic, structural, and other deterministic causes including implicit bias and structural racism. Students will be taught how to access interpret public-access injury and violence data, and as identify the magnitude of the problem to the degree that it is known, based on peer- reviewed literature and other resources. In addition, they will learn how to identify and prioritize injury/violence problems based on specific sub-populations, and also how to assess the consequences of injury & violence to individuals, families, and communities by integrating information from peer-reviewed literature. The course will also critique strategies to prevent injury and violence. Finally, students will have the opportunity to focus on one specific injury/violence topic and delve into its problem, causes, and public health intervention/prevention best practices.
